title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Realistic Scenarios Through Representation Engineering
summary: Studies dynamic representation interventions for reducing reward hacking in tool-using, long-context tasks.
caveat: Reported capability preservation and cross-domain transfer are limited to the tested settings; no blanket deployment guarantee.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Reward Misspecification Degrades Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
summary: Studies how optimizing misspecified rewards can make reasoning traces less revealing of reward hacks, and tests training that makes reward descriptions explicit.
caveat: The experiments use three models and three tasks; reported mitigation gains should not be generalized to every model or monitoring setup.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Act on Your Behalf, Beyond Your Authorization: Benchmarking LLM Agent Authorization Alignment
summary: Introduces AuthorizationBench to distinguish completing a task from respecting the actions the user actually authorized.
caveat: Benchmark rates describe particular model-and-harness configurations, not the rate of unauthorized actions in general deployment.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Instructions Are Evidence, Not Objectives: Measuring Outcome Alignment of Agents
summary: Introduces tasks with discoverable but initially unstated requirements to test whether agents deliver the intended outcome rather than only obey the initial wording.
caveat: Inferring missing requirements is not permission to take consequential actions outside the user’s authorization.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Gradient Routing Localizes and Removes Unintended Behaviors in RL
summary: GRAFT routes gradients from flagged training samples into removable parameters, aiming to reduce unintended behavior without teaching the model to hide it from a reward penalty.
caveat: The approach depends on its monitoring and parameter-isolation setup; results are not evidence of complete alignment.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.
